fields.name: Four Seasons Hotel Beirut
fields.description: Luxury 5-star hotel on the Beirut waterfront with stunning Mediterranean views.

fields.name: Phoenicia Hotel Beirut
fields.description: Iconic landmark hotel in the heart of Beirut, offering world-class hospitality since 1961.

fields.name: Mövenpick Hotel Beirut
fields.description: Contemporary hotel near Beirut city center with panoramic views.

fields.name: Intercontinental Mzaar
fields.description: Mountain resort hotel in Mzaar Kfardebian, Lebanon's top ski destination.

fields.name: Byblos Sur Mer
fields.description: Charming hotel by the ancient port of Byblos, one of the world's oldest cities.

fields.name: Le Gray Beirut
fields.description: Award-winning boutique hotel in Downtown Beirut with rooftop pool.

fields.name: Em Sherif
fields.description: Award-winning Lebanese cuisine in an elegant setting, considered one of the best in the Middle East.

fields.name: Tawlet
fields.description: Farm-to-table Lebanese restaurant run by rural women cooperatives, unique menu daily.

fields.name: Liza Beirut
fields.description: Sophisticated Lebanese cuisine in a stunning 1930s mansion in Achrafieh.

fields.name: Babel Restaurant
fields.description: Rooftop dining with panoramic Beirut views, serving contemporary Lebanese cuisine.

fields.name: Leila Restaurant
fields.description: Traditional Lebanese home cooking in a warm, authentic atmosphere.

fields.name: Mounir Restaurant
fields.description: Famous grill restaurant in Zahle, known for its mezze and grilled meats by the river.

fields.name: Aleph Restaurant
fields.description: Trendy Beirut bistro blending Lebanese and Mediterranean flavors in Gemmayze.

fields.name: Mayrig
fields.description: Authentic Armenian cuisine in Bourj Hammoud, beloved for its traditional recipes.

fields.name: Baalbek Roman Temples
fields.description: One of the best preserved Roman temple complexes in the world, featuring the Temple of Jupiter and Temple of Bacchus.

fields.name: Jeita Grotto
fields.description: Stunning limestone caves with underground river, one of the natural wonders of the world.

fields.name: Byblos Ancient City
fields.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, with Phoenician, Roman, and Crusader ruins.

fields.name: Cedars of God
fields.description: Ancient cedar forest in Bcharre, one of the last remaining forests of the Lebanon Cedar, sacred trees mentioned in the Bible.

fields.name: Pigeon Rocks Beirut
fields.description: Natural arch rock formations off the coast of Raouche, Beirut's most iconic landmark.

fields.name: Qadisha Valley
fields.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site — a sacred valley with ancient monasteries carved into cliffs.

fields.name: National Museum of Beirut
fields.description: Lebanon's principal public museum, housing artifacts from prehistoric times to the medieval period.

fields.name: Tyre Archaeological Site
fields.description: UNESCO World Heritage Site with Roman hippodrome, necropolis, and Crusader ruins.

fields.name: Our Lady of Lebanon
fields.description: Famous Marian shrine in Harissa, with a giant statue visible from Beirut and the sea.

fields.name: Sidon Sea Castle
fields.description: 13th-century Crusader fortress built on a small island connected to the mainland by a bridge.

fields.name: Anjar Umayyad City
fields.description: Anjar, also known as Hawsh Mousa, is a town of Lebanon, near the Syrian border, located in the Bekaa Valley. The population is 2,400, consisting almost entirely of Armenians. The total area is about twenty square kilometers.

fields.name: Beiteddine Palace
fields.description: Beiteddine Palace is an 18th-century palace in Beiteddine, Lebanon, built by Bashir II. The palace hosts the annual Beiteddine Festival and the Beiteddine Palace Museum. and is also the residence of the President of Lebanon during the summer.

fields.name: Deir el Qamar
fields.description: Deir al-Qamar is a city south-east of Beirut in south-central Lebanon. It is located five kilometres outside of Beit ed-Dine in the Chouf District of the Mount Lebanon Governorate at 800 m of average altitude.

fields.name: Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque
fields.description: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, also referred to as the Blue Mosque, is a Sunni mosque, 72 m high, minarets´ roof of 65 m high and main dome spire of 48 m high and its roof 42 m, is located in downtown Beirut, Lebanon. In the 19th century, a zawiya was built on this site.

fields.name: Sursock Museum
fields.description: The Sursock Museum, officially known as the Nicolas Ibrahim Sursock Museum, is a modern and contemporary art museum in Beirut, Lebanon.

fields.name: Tripoli Citadel
fields.description: The Citadel of Tripoli is a 12th-century fortress in Tripoli, Lebanon. It was built at the top of a hill "during the initial Frankish siege of the city between 1102 and 1109" on the orders of Raymond de Saint-Gilles, who baptized it the Castle of Mount Pilgrim while local Muslims have been referring to it as the Castle...

fields.name: Gibran Museum
fields.description: The Gibran Museum, formerly the Monastery of Mar Sarkis, is a biographical museum in Bsharri, Lebanon, 120 kilometres from Beirut. It is dedicated to the Lebanese writer, philosopher, and artist Kahlil Gibran. The museum was an old cavern where many hermits sought refuge since the 7th century.

fields.name: Horsh Ehden Nature Reserve
fields.description: Horsh Ehden is a nature reserve located in Northern Lebanon. It contains a forest of the cedar of Lebanon, making it a part of the country's cultural and natural heritage.

fields.name: Baatara Gorge Waterfall
fields.description: The Baatara gorge sinkhole is a waterfall in the Batroun district of Lebanon near the village of Chatine in the town of Tannourine. The waterfall drops 255 metres into the Balaa Pothole, a cave of Jurassic limestone located on the Lebanon Mountain Trail. The cave is also known as the Cave of the Three Bridges.

fields.name: Batroun
fields.description: Batroun, is a coastal city in northern Lebanon and one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. It is the capital city of Batroun District.

fields.name: Mansouri Great Mosque
fields.description: The Mansouri Great Mosque is a mosque in Tripoli, Lebanon. It was built in the Mamluk period, from 1294 to 1298. This was the first building to be erected in Mamluk Tripoli.

fields.name: Ksara Winery
fields.description: Château Ksara is a winery in Beqaa Valley of Lebanon. it is located in the town of Ksara near Zahle. It was founded in 1857 by Jesuit priests.

fields.name: Beaufort Castle
fields.description: Beaufort or Belfort Castle, known locally as Qal'at al-Shaqif or Shaqif Arnun, is a Crusader fortress in Nabatieh Governorate, Southern Lebanon, about 1 kilometre to the south-south-east of the village of Arnoun.

fields.name: Saint George Maronite Cathedral
fields.description: Saint George Maronite Cathedral is the cathedral of the Maronite Catholic Archeparchy of Beirut, located in downtown Beirut, Lebanon. Constructed between 1884 and 1894 under Archbishop Joseph Debs, the cathedral stands on the site of an earlier 18th-century church dedicated to Saint George.

fields.name: Beirut Souks
fields.description: Beirut Souks is a commercial district located in the Beirut Central District. It comprises more than 200 retail outlets, approximately 25 restaurants and cafés, an entertainment center, a 14-screen cinema complex, periodic street markets, and a planned department store.

fields.name: Tyre Coast Nature Reserve
fields.description: The Tyre Coast Nature Reserve is a nature reserve and a Ramsar site southeast of Tyre, Lebanon. Covering an area of over 380 hectares, it is bisected by the Rashidieh refugee camp.

fields.name: Mseilha Fort
fields.description: The Mseilha Fort is a historic fortification located in Northern Lebanon, strategically positioned on the right bank of Nahr al-Jaouz river, in Hamat, approximately 2.5 kilometers northeast of the city of Batroun in North Lebanon.

fields.name: Aammiq Wetland
fields.description: The Aammiq Wetland is the largest remaining freshwater wetland in Lebanon, a remnant of much more extensive marshes and lakes that once existed in the Bekaa Valley.

fields.name: Zahle
fields.description: Zahlé is a city in eastern Lebanon, and the capital and largest city of Beqaa Governorate, Lebanon. With around 150,000 inhabitants, it is the third-largest city in Lebanon after Beirut and Tripoli and the fourth-largest taking the whole urban area.

fields.name: Casino du Liban
fields.description: Casino du Liban is a casino located in Jounieh, Lebanon, 22 km north of Beirut. The casino is managed by Metropolitan Gaming, a subsidiary of Silver Point Capital.

fields.name: Jabal Moussa Biosphere Reserve
fields.description: Jabal Moussa Biosphere Reserve is a nature reserve located in the Keserwan District of Lebanon, on the shoulders of the western slopes of Mount Lebanon overlooking the Mediterranean Sea to the West.

fields.name: Qurnat as Sawda
fields.description: Qurnat as Sawdā is the highest point in Lebanon and the Levant, at 3,088 m above sea level. It is the summit of Jabal al Makmel, a mountain range in Bsharri, North Lebanon.

fields.name: Bsharri
fields.description: Bsharri is a Lebanese town located in the district of the same name, North Governorate, situated at altitudes between 1,100 m and 3,088 m. Bsharri is the location of the Cedars of God, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the only remaining place where the Cedrus libani tree grows natively.

fields.name: Jounieh
fields.description: Jounieh is a coastal city in Keserwan District, about 16 km north of Beirut, Lebanon. Since 2017, it has been the capital of Keserwan-Jbeil Governorate.

fields.name: Qadisha Valley Hiking
fields.description: Trek through the UNESCO-listed Qadisha Valley, one of the most dramatic gorges in Lebanon with ancient monasteries carved into cliffs.

fields.name: Cedars Ski Resort
fields.description: Ski on Lebanon's oldest ski resort surrounded by the ancient Cedars of God forest. Open December to April.

fields.name: Jeita Grotto Boat Ride
fields.description: Take a boat ride through the lower cave of Jeita Grotto, gliding along an underground river surrounded by stunning stalactites.

fields.name: Baalbek Temple Tour
fields.description: Guided tour of the Roman temples of Baalbek, including the Temple of Jupiter and Temple of Bacchus with expert local guides.

fields.name: Byblos Snorkeling
fields.description: Snorkel in the crystal-clear waters of Byblos along the ancient Phoenician coast, discovering underwater ruins and marine life.

fields.name: Beirut Nightlife Tour
fields.description: Experience Beirut's legendary nightlife with a guided tour of Gemmayzeh, Mar Mikhael and Downtown's best bars and clubs.

fields.name: Harissa Cable Car
fields.description: Take the famous cable car (teleferique) from Jounieh bay up to the Our Lady of Lebanon shrine in Harissa with panoramic views.

fields.name: Tyre Beach Day
fields.description: Relax on the stunning sandy beaches of Tyre, one of the best beaches in Lebanon near the UNESCO archaeological site.

fields.name: Shouf Cedar Reserve Hiking
fields.description: Hike through the Shouf Cedar Biosphere Reserve, the largest nature reserve in Lebanon with ancient cedar trees and wildlife.

fields.name: Sidon Soap Museum Tour
fields.description: Visit the famous Sidon Soap Museum housed in a 19th-century soap factory, exploring Lebanon's traditional soap-making heritage.
